Types of tourism & reasons to travel.front: Name the main reasons people travel
Types of tourism & reasons to travel.back: Leisure (holiday), business, visiting friends and relatives (VFR), and special interest (health, education, religion, sport).
Travelling for tourism within your own country.
Visitors from other countries coming into a country.
Residents leaving their own country to travel abroad.
Responsible travel to natural areas that conserves the environment and supports local people.

Types of tourism & reasons to travel.front: Give two examples of special-interest tourism
Types of tourism & reasons to travel.back: Dive tourism, wellness/spa tourism, adventure tourism, cultural tourism.

Sustainable tourism.back: Tourism that meets the needs of visitors and hosts today without harming the environment, culture or economy for the future.

Sustainable tourism.front: Give two ways a resort can reduce its environmental impact
Sustainable tourism.back: Solar power, desalination with renewable energy, banning single-use plastics, reef-safe activities.

Sustainable tourism.front: How can tourism support local communities sustainably?
Sustainable tourism.back: Employ and train local staff, buy local produce, support local crafts and community projects.
The maximum number of visitors a place can take before damage or a poor experience results.

Sustainable tourism.front: Example of visitor management for sustainability
Sustainable tourism.back: Limiting numbers, fixed paths, zoning, entry fees, guided tours.

Types of tourists & destinations.back: Families, couples, business travellers, backpackers, groups, older travellers, adventure seekers.

Types of tourists & destinations.front: What does a family with young children need?
Types of tourists & destinations.back: Child-friendly facilities, safety, family rooms, kids' clubs and activities.
Coastal/island, city, rural/countryside, mountain, heritage, purpose-built resorts.
A destination built mainly for tourists, such as a resort island or theme park.

Types of tourists & destinations.front: Why might honeymoon couples choose the Maldives?
Types of tourists & destinations.back: Privacy, luxury overwater villas, romantic setting, beaches and spa services.
Wi-Fi, meeting rooms, airport transfers, convenient location, flexible check-in.

Global tourism.front: Give three factors that have increased global tourism
Global tourism.back: Cheaper flights, more disposable income, more paid holidays, internet booking, better transport.

Global tourism.front: Why can global events reduce tourism?
Global tourism.back: Pandemics, conflict, natural disasters and economic recessions reduce demand and travel.
A long flight, usually over 6 hours, often between continents.
Places that have recently started to attract more tourists.

Global tourism.front: How does exchange rate affect tourism?
Global tourism.back: A weak local currency makes the destination cheaper for visitors, so demand may rise.

Global tourism.front: Give one reason tourism is seasonal
Global tourism.back: Weather, school holidays and festivals change demand at different times of year.

Destination appeal.back: Natural attractions, built attractions, culture, events, accessibility, accommodation, safety and climate.
Beaches, coral reefs, mountains, wildlife, lagoons.
Museums, theme parks, historic buildings, shopping malls.
Easy, affordable transport and visas make it simpler for visitors to come.
Festivals and sports events attract visitors at specific times and give publicity.

Destination appeal.front: What is a unique selling point (USP)?
Destination appeal.back: A feature that makes a destination different from competitors, e.g. house reef diving.

Managing destinations.back: To protect resources, control impacts, keep visitors satisfied and share benefits.
Zoning, limits on numbers, pricing, signs and education, timed tickets, marked trails.
Dividing an area into parts with different permitted uses, e.g. a protected reef zone.

Managing destinations.front: Role of the government in destination management
Managing destinations.back: Planning, regulation, licensing, infrastructure and marketing.

Managing destinations.front: What is a code of conduct for tourists?
Managing destinations.back: Guidelines on good behaviour, e.g. not touching coral, dressing respectfully.
They reduce crowding and raise money for conservation.

Impacts of tourism.back: Jobs, foreign currency, tax income, growth of local businesses, multiplier effect.
Leakage, seasonal jobs, low wages, rising prices, over-dependence on tourism.
Money from tourism that leaves the country, e.g. imported food or foreign-owned resorts.
Pride in culture, revival of crafts, better facilities for locals, cultural exchange.
Loss of traditions, conflict over dress or behaviour, crime, staged authenticity.
Coral damage, waste, pollution, habitat loss, water shortage, carbon emissions.
Money for conservation, protected areas, environmental awareness.

Tourism organisations.back: Owned or run by the government, e.g. a national tourism board.
Owned by individuals or companies and aims to make a profit, e.g. resorts and airlines.
Not-for-profit groups, e.g. charities protecting the environment.

Tourism organisations.front: What does a national tourism organisation do?
Tourism organisations.back: Promotes the country, gives visitor information, sets standards and collects data.

Tourism organisations.front: What does a tour operator do?
Tourism organisations.back: Puts together package holidays (transport, accommodation, activities).

Tourism organisations.front: What does a travel agent do?
Tourism organisations.back: Sells travel products to customers and gives advice.

Transport & infrastructure.back: Air, sea (ferries, speedboats, cruises), land (bus, car hire, train).
Basic services a destination needs: airports, roads, water, power, telecommunications, waste systems.

Transport & infrastructure.front: Why is a seaplane useful in the Maldives?
Transport & infrastructure.back: It links the main airport to distant resort islands quickly, with views as an extra attraction.

Transport & infrastructure.front: How does better infrastructure help tourism?
Transport & infrastructure.back: It improves access, comfort and safety, so more visitors can come.

Customer service.back: Meeting and exceeding customers' needs and expectations.
Listen, apologise, find a solution, act, then follow up.
Repeat visits, good reviews, word-of-mouth, higher sales, motivated staff.
Listening, clear communication, product knowledge, positive body language, patience.

Customer service.front: Name types of customers with special needs
Customer service.back: Guests with disabilities, families with infants, non-native speakers, older travellers.
To keep standards high and give consistent, confident service.

Marketing mix.back: The holiday or service: accommodation, activities, experiences.
Penetration, skimming, premium, discount, seasonal and promotional pricing.
How the product is distributed or sold: direct online, travel agents, tour operators.
Social media, websites, brochures, advertising, familiarisation (fam) trips, trade fairs.
Higher prices in peak season and lower prices in low season.

Market research & segmentation.back: Collecting information about customers and competitors to make better decisions.
Questionnaires, interviews, guest feedback forms, focus groups.
Government statistics, reports, online reviews, competitor websites.
Dividing customers into groups with similar needs, e.g. by age, income or interests.
To target the right customers with the right product and promotion.
